text:
Marina: follow-up on the canary fallback RFC: per-tenant scoring vs global budget — pros/cons?
Devon: per-tenant. saw a noisy tenant kill a canary before.
Alex: per-tenant adds state, need fast lookups. local cache?
Marina: hybrid: runtime keeps small sliding windows & consults control-plane policies. decisions cached for 10s.
Ira: bound state size. evict LRU tenants and expose eviction metrics.
Nina: confidence is noisy; use smoothed percentile deltas vs baseline.
Sam: also require min-requests threshold so tiny tenants don't flip decisions.
Alex: policy blob idea: conditions+weights+threshold+cooldown (small JSON blob).
Ira: include cooldown_jitter to avoid flip-flop.
Devon: need reason header for routed requests: X-Canary-Decision: fallback(reason=conf_delta).
Sam: runtime emits per-tenant fallback counters to metrics and reason as last_decision label.
Marina: ownership: control-plane = policy lifecycle, runtime = scoring/enforcement. client-side routing = future opt-in only.
Nina: design scoring pipeline (transforms->aggregators->evaluator) so ML can swap signals.
Marina: rollout plan: proto schema -> local eval proto -> small tenant pilot -> 2 week observation -> widen. kill-switch mandatory.
deploy-bot: RFC draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/canary-tenant-fallback-2026-draft (auto)
